narrativeReportMd:
# ImmunizationEvaluation R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ImmunizationEvaluation` appears to have been removed from the supplied R6 ballot core package. This is a hard R4-to-R6 instance break: an R4 resource with `resourceType: "ImmunizationEvaluation"` has no R6 StructureDefinition to validate against, no same-name resource type in the R6 package index, and no clear local replacement.

## Scope
The assessment compared the R4 StructureDefinition, R4 local terminology artifacts, R4/R6 package indexes, package metadata, and the R6 `Immunization` resource as a possible partial migration target. Base `DomainResource`/`Resource` inheritance changes and separate artifacts such as search parameters are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The dominant issue is artifact identity/removal rather than a narrow element-level delta. R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` carried a separate clinical evaluation record with mandatory `status`, `patient`, `targetDisease`, `immunizationEvent`, and `doseStatus`. R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` preserves some protocol metadata such as `series`, `authority`, `targetDisease`, `doseNumber`, and `seriesDoses`, but it does not provide a standard place for the evaluation record's status, evaluation date, dose-validity result, validity reasons, or a first-class resource identity.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `ImmunizationEvaluation:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:83a7e2b1`: R4 instances of the resource become invalid or unrecognized under the supplied R6 core definitions. The main migration risk is lossless representation of dose-validity semantics, covered by `ImmunizationEvaluation:CONVERSION_OR_MAPPING:root:1f7cd957` and `ImmunizationEvaluation:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:doseStatus:8dba1882`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to choose an R6 representation. Options include profile-specific extensions, an `Observation`-based evaluation, a retained/custom `Basic` or extension-backed resource, or a jurisdictional profile of `Immunization`; the local package files do not identify an official replacement.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design could have retained a deprecated R6 resource or supplied a normative cross-version extension/profile and ConceptMap. Without those artifacts, migration is not just a syntactic rename; it requires clinical and interoperability policy decisions.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze R6 `Immunization`, relevant immunization terminology, and any official ballot change notes or conversion maps before selecting a production migration strategy.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ImmunizationEvaluation` is absent from the supplied R6 ballot package, so R4 instances are not directly valid R6 instances. The top migration concerns are resource-type removal, lack of a lossless standard R6 target for evaluation semantics, and loss of the R4 dose-status terminology bindings as first-class resource elements. Confidence is high for absence/removal and medium for intended replacement because official narrative diff material was not supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a resource retirement/conversion problem, not an in-place version update. Systems must identify all R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` records, decide whether evaluation results become extensions, observations, local profiles, or retained legacy records, and validate that dose validity and reason semantics remain queryable and clinically visible. Any partial use of `Immunization.protocolApplied` only carries protocol context; it does not by itself preserve the evaluation outcome.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: The core finding has high confidence because the expected R6 StructureDefinition file is absent, the R6 package index has no matching entry, and broad local searches found no `ImmunizationEvaluation` resource. Confidence about the intended replacement is lower because the supplied inputs do not include official narrative diffs, change notes, or cross-version ConceptMaps.

findings.title: ImmunizationEvaluation resource is absent from the R6 core package

semanticText.definition: Describes a comparison of an immunization event against published recommendations to determine if the administration is "valid" in relation to those recommendations.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `ImmunizationEvaluation` is a first-class resource derived from `DomainResource`. Its local differential includes identifiers and mandatory evaluation fields such as `status`, `patient`, `targetDisease`, `immunizationEvent`, and `doseStatus`.

newState.summary: No R6 `ImmunizationEvaluation` StructureDefinition or package-index entry was found.
newState.narrativeMd: The supplied R6 core package has no `StructureDefinition-ImmunizationEvaluation.json`; its package index contains no `ImmunizationEvaluation` StructureDefinition entry; local searches did not find an obvious same-resource rename or split target.

facts.note: The expected R6 file path is absent.
The R4 resource-types code system includes the code; the supplied R6 resource-type value set did not expose a matching code in the local search.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match check started with the canonical same-name file and package-index row, then searched R6 package contents for `ImmunizationEvaluation` and related evaluation phrases. The only closely related R6 StructureDefinition found was `Immunization`, which lacks evaluation-outcome elements and is therefore only a partial migration target, not a same-resource replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. An R4 instance whose `resourceType` is `ImmunizationEvaluation` has no R6 resource definition in the supplied package, so strict validators, serializers, generated model libraries, REST endpoint routing, and resource-type enum switches can reject or fail to recognize it. This is broader than an element-level constraint: the whole resource type disappears from the R6 core package.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource represents clinical/public-health dose-validity determinations. Losing a standard representation can affect immunization forecasting, schedule compliance review, and public-health reporting if systems do not define a replacement.

justification.inferredGoal: The model may have intended to retire or consolidate separate dose-evaluation records, but the local package evidence does not explain the rationale.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `ImmunizationEvaluation` in base R6 as a deprecated or trial-use resource while steering new implementations to any successor pattern.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Retiring or consolidating a low-maturity evaluation resource may be a reasonable R6 goal, but the supplied R6 package removes the resource without a same-resource definition or visible standard replacement. A base R6 design that kept the R4 resource shape as deprecated would have preserved existing instances, validators, generated classes, and REST routing while still allowing the specification to recommend a newer model. Because that less-breaking path appears practical and the local evidence does not show why removal was necessary, the level of breakage looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest backward-compatible base design would keep `ImmunizationEvaluation` as a concrete R6 StructureDefinition, probably flagged deprecated/trial-use with clear guidance that new systems should prefer the successor approach. That preserves most or all R4-valid instances because the resource type and its required evaluation fields remain available. The main tradeoff is long-term specification and implementation burden: if R6 also introduces or recommends another representation, both may coexist indefinitely and systems may need policies to prevent divergent duplicate evaluation records.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps legacy resource surface and may create duplicate representations if a successor model exists, but preserves R4 instances and typed APIs.

evidence.detail: R4 describes the resource as a comparison of an immunization event against recommendations to determine validity.
The expected R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
No R6 package-index entry matched filename, id, or URL containing `ImmunizationEvaluation`.
R6 `Immunization` has protocol-related elements but no `doseStatus`, `doseStatusReason`, or separate evaluation record identity.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment includes the R4-required local elements. It is illustrative rather than a complete standalone clinical record; the key compatibility point is that `resourceType: "ImmunizationEvaluation"` has no R6 resource definition in the supplied package.

findings.narrativeMd: `ImmunizationEvaluation` was a separate R4 resource for recording whether an immunization dose counted against published recommendations. In the supplied R6 ballot package, the resource is absent rather than changed in place. Existing R4 data, APIs, generated classes, and FHIRPath/search logic that expect this resource type cannot move to R6 by simple validation against updated definitions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `ImmunizationEvaluation` instance becomes invalid or unrecognized in R6 because the resource type itself is not defined. This affects strict validators, JSON/XML parsers with generated resource enums, REST servers exposing typed endpoints, subscription/topic logic keyed by resource type, and persistence layers using resource-specific tables. There is no R6-to-R4 issue for same-resource instances because the R6 resource is absent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` records and consumers before upgrading. Do not merely drop the resource: decide an explicit R6 representation, preserve links to the evaluated `Immunization`, retain evaluation outcome and reason semantics, and update API/search/codegen layers. If no official replacement is available, use a governed extension/profile or retained legacy store and add tests that an example R4 record either converts losslessly or is intentionally quarantined.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal could have been less disruptive if R6 retained the resource as deprecated or provided a standard replacement artifact and conversion map. Those alternatives preserve old validation and interoperability at the cost of keeping legacy model surface. Because no such artifact is visible in the supplied package, the change is not backward compatible for existing instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 ballot narrative or change notes before finalizing production guidance. The local package evidence is sufficient for validation impact but not for standards-process rationale.

findings.title: No lossless standard R6 mapping target is evident for the evaluation record

oldState.summary: R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` is an independent evaluation resource tied to a patient and immunization event.

semanticText.definition: The R4 resource records a comparison of an immunization event against recommendations, including evaluation status, date, authority, target disease, immunization event, dose status, dose-status reasons, description, series, dose number, and series doses.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 local content model separates the act of evaluating a dose from the underlying administered immunization. It can carry its own identifier, lifecycle status, date, authority, outcome, and reasons.

newState.summary: R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` carries some protocol metadata but not the full evaluation record.

semanticText.definition: R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` describes the protocol followed by the provider who administered the dose. It includes optional `series`, `authority`, `targetDisease`, `doseNumber`, and `seriesDoses`, but not evaluation status or dose-validity result.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Immunization` has useful partial overlap for protocol context, but it is embedded in the immunization event and does not represent a separate evaluation with a validity outcome.

facts.note: The R6 element describes the disease the dose is administered against, not necessarily the disease the dose was evaluated against.
A migration using this target requires type conversion and coding policy.
No standard R6 Immunization element was found for valid/not-valid evaluation outcome and reasons.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` is the nearest local structural overlap because it carries series, authority, target disease, dose number, and series doses. It is not a true successor because it lacks the separate evaluation resource identity, the evaluated-event reference, evaluation date/status, and validity outcome/reason fields.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The artifact removal is the direct hard validation break; this finding captures the migration/conversion risk after implementers choose a replacement. Some R4 fields can be copied into `Immunization.protocolApplied`, but core evaluation facts cannot. Without a governed mapping, converters may silently drop dose-validity conclusions or conflate provider-intended protocol metadata with retrospective evaluation results.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dose validity can drive immunization forecasting and clinical/public-health decisions. A lossy mapping may make an invalid dose look merely administered or may hide why it did not count.

justification.inferredGoal: Possible consolidation of protocol-related immunization data into `Immunization`, with separate evaluation semantics left to profiles or other resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Provide a base R6 successor model for the evaluation outcome or temporarily retain the old resource; profile, extension, or converter-only guidance is only a mitigation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The nearby R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` structure only carries protocol metadata and does not represent the separate evaluation lifecycle, evaluated-event relationship, dose-validity result, or reasons. Consolidating immunization-related data may be reasonable, but omitting a lossless standard target leaves implementers to invent incompatible mappings for clinically meaningful evaluation data. The available less-breaking designs have real tradeoffs, so they are only partial alternatives, but the absence of any visible standard mapping target is not clearly justified by the local evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have added a first-class R6 evaluation backbone or successor resource covering `date`, `immunizationEvent`, `doseStatus`, `doseStatusReason`, and separate evaluation identity, or it could have retained `ImmunizationEvaluation` for a transition period. Those are base-design alternatives, unlike a ConceptMap, converter, profile, or extension-only package. They would still require careful governance because evaluation facts could be represented both on the old resource and in the new structure, and optional successor elements may not preserve every R4 workflow or search/API expectation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A core successor or retained legacy resource would reduce data loss but creates duplicate same-fact representations, validation ambiguity, and implementation burden.

evidence.detail: R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` is an optional repeating backbone for the protocol followed by the provider who administered the dose.
R6 `doseNumber` under `protocolApplied` is `CodeableConcept`, not the R4 `positiveInt|string` choice used by `ImmunizationEvaluation.doseNumber[x]`.
No R6 `Immunization` element with `doseStatus`, `doseStatusReason`, or equivalent evaluation-outcome naming was found in the local element search.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows only a partial mapping to R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied`. It intentionally has no place for the R4 evaluation result `doseStatus=valid` or detailed `doseStatusReason`; those would require a policy-specific extension, profile, or alternate resource.

findings.narrativeMd: Even after choosing `Immunization` as a nearby R6 target, the R4 resource is not losslessly representable. The R4 resource is about an evaluation result; R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` is about the protocol associated with administration. Conflating the two can change clinical meaning and break applications that distinguish original administration data from retrospective validity assessment.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a separate same-resource validation rule because the direct break is the missing R6 resource. It is a conversion compatibility risk: a syntactically valid R6 `Immunization` created from R4 data may omit or misrepresent the R4 evaluation outcome. Generated converters and ETL jobs need explicit handling rather than field-name matching.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a mapping table for every R4 local element. Treat `series`, `authority`, `targetDisease`, `doseNumber[x]`, and `seriesDoses[x]` as only partial candidates for `Immunization.protocolApplied`. Preserve `identifier`, `status`, `date`, `patient`, `immunizationEvent`, `doseStatus`, `doseStatusReason`, and `description` through extensions, related resources, or a retained legacy store unless official R6 guidance supplies another target. Test both valid and not-valid dose evaluations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have supplied an explicit successor model or retained the old resource long enough to allow gradual migration. The partial structural overlap in `Immunization` is not enough because it lacks the evaluation result and lifecycle semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: If official R6 narrative recommends `Observation` or a specific extension for immunization evaluation, this finding should be updated to reference that replacement and reassess losslessness.

findings.title: Dose-validity status and reason terminology are no longer first-class fields on a standard R6 resource

oldState.summary: R4 has standard terminology bindings for evaluation lifecycle status, dose validity, and dose-validity reasons.

binding.description: `status` is required-bound to completed/entered-in-error; `doseStatus` and `doseStatusReason` have example bindings to evaluation-specific code systems.

semanticText.definition: `doseStatus` indicates if the dose is valid or not valid with respect to published recommendations; `doseStatusReason` explains why.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 gives evaluation outcomes standard element names and terminology hooks, including the codes `valid` and `notvalid` for whether a dose counts.

newState.summary: No R6 `ImmunizationEvaluation` element or local same-name R6 terminology binding was found.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local R6 package searches did not find `immunization-evaluation-*` value sets or code systems. External terminology package status was not evaluated.

newState.narrativeMd: Because the resource is absent, the R4 evaluation-specific bindings are not carried as first-class fields in the R6 core resource model. R6 `Immunization.status` and `statusReason` describe the immunization event, not whether an administered dose counted against recommendations.

facts.note: The R4 local CodeSystem defines `valid` and `notvalid`; no same first-class R6 field was found in the supplied package.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old terminology belongs to local R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` elements. R6 `Immunization.status` uses immunization-event status and is not a semantic match for evaluation dose validity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The hard validation break is already captured by resource removal. The terminology-specific risk is semantic and runtime: decision-support, forecasting, reporting, and analytics code often switch on `doseStatus` values such as `valid` and `notvalid`. If migration drops those codes or maps them to ordinary immunization event status, systems can change behavior without a validator error.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly preserving or losing dose-validity status can affect whether additional vaccination is recommended or whether a dose is counted for compliance.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly to remove evaluation-specific terminology from the core resource set or move it to another artifact.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a first-class R6 path for dose-validity status/reasons with the R4 bindings, either on a retained resource or a core successor element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Dose-validity status is clinically meaningful and is not equivalent to `Immunization.status` or `statusReason`. The local R6 package does not show a first-class replacement for the R4 `valid`/`notvalid` outcome and reason bindings. Removing the standard paths and bindings may support a broader resource retirement goal, but without a visible base R6 successor it leaves safety-relevant semantics to local conventions. Because a base design could have preserved those semantics, the terminology loss is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could retain `ImmunizationEvaluation.doseStatus` and `doseStatusReason` with their bindings, or add equivalent core R6 elements in a successor model and bind them to the same or explicitly mapped code systems. Merely publishing an extension, ConceptMap, or migration guide would be a mitigation rather than a backward-compatible base design. The partial tradeoff is that first-class retained terminology may perpetuate an old modeling choice and create two places to encode the same dose-validity conclusion if a new model also exists.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves semantic continuity but may carry legacy terminology and duplicate outcome representations if R6 intended to move evaluation outside core.

evidence.detail: R4 `status` has a required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/immunization-evaluation-status|4.0.1`.
R4 `doseStatus` has an example binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/immunization-evaluation-dose-status`.
The R4 dose-status code system defines `valid` and `notvalid`.
The R4 reason code system includes reason codes such as `advstorage`, `coldchbrk`, `explot`, `outsidesched`, and `prodrecall`.
R6 `Immunization.status` describes the immunization event (`completed | entered-in-error | not-done`), not a dose-validity evaluation outcome.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows why mapping to `Immunization.status` would be wrong: `status=completed` says the evaluation record is complete, while `doseStatus=notvalid` says the administered dose does not count.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource removal also removes standard element-level hooks for evaluation-specific terminology. The most clinically significant value is `doseStatus`, which distinguishes doses that count from those that do not. This is not equivalent to the status of the immunization event itself.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with these codes are already invalid in R6 because the resource is absent. More subtly, a converted R6 artifact can be valid while no longer carrying the coded conclusion or reason. That affects enum switches, measure logic, forecasting rules, and analytics that formerly depended on standard paths and code systems.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve `doseStatus` and `doseStatusReason` explicitly during migration. If using extensions, bind them to the original code systems or an officially mapped successor and keep the evaluated `Immunization` link. Do not map `doseStatus=notvalid` to `Immunization.status=entered-in-error` or `not-done`; those statuses have different meanings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have kept the terminology artifacts and exposed a standard R6 path for evaluation outcome. Without that, implementations must create local conventions, which increases interoperability risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology confidence would improve by checking the current external THO package and any R6 narrative guidance for retained or renamed immunization-evaluation code systems.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` differential did not define local invariants beyond the standard inherited resource/datatype constraints. No separate local constraint strengthening or weakening was identified apart from the resource's removal.
No local slicing or slices were present in the R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` differential.
No local fixed values, pattern values, or default values were identified in the R4 differential.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were identified in the R4 differential.

R4 local references target `Patient`, `Organization`, and `Immunization`. Because no R6 `ImmunizationEvaluation` counterpart exists, there is no same-element reference-target narrowing or widening to report separately from removal.

The R4 local type model was checked. Element-level type deltas are subsumed by the absent R6 artifact; the only partial migration target found changes the possible dose-number representation to `CodeableConcept` under `Immunization.protocolApplied`.

R4 local cardinalities were reviewed. There is no same-resource R6 cardinality comparison because the R6 resource is absent; mandatory R4 fields are therefore affected through resource removal rather than a local min/max edit.
R4 `status` is a local modifier element. No standalone modifier-flag flip exists because the entire R6 resource is absent; inherited modifier-extension flag changes are out of scope.

R4 summary flags on local fields such as `status`, `patient`, `targetDisease`, `immunizationEvent`, and `doseStatus` were checked. Their loss is covered by resource removal, not by an independent summary-flag change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Immunization retains optional protocol metadata that can support partial migration
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a direct change to `ImmunizationEvaluation` and does not make old `ImmunizationEvaluation` instances valid in R6. It is notable because it may preserve some non-outcome metadata if a migration strategy embeds evaluation context into `Immunization`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: `series`, `authority`, `targetDisease`, `doseNumber`, and `seriesDoses` may be useful partial targets, but `doseNumber`/`seriesDoses` use `CodeableConcept` in R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` and the evaluation result fields still need another representation.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Immunization` is the closest local structural overlap and should be assessed as a migration target, including its own R4-to-R6 changes.
Dose-validity codes are central to preserving clinical meaning. Confirm whether these code systems and associated value sets remain in external terminology packages or have official successors.
R4 package index includes multiple `ImmunizationEvaluation` search parameters. Their R6 absence or replacement affects API migration but is outside this StructureDefinition-focused report.
Inherited base-resource changes are intentionally excluded here and should be handled by the base-artifact report if material.
